relevance_note: Case report of a boy with PAPA syndrome and a PSTPIP1 variant ("identified a heterozygous PSTPIP1 c.770A>G (p.Glu257Gly) variant"), his carrier father and tested-negative mother, plus a literature table (Table 2) of 20 previously published PAPA patients.
method_note: Read in full by hand. Table 2 (literature review, no label column) was transcribed by a short Python script splitting each row into its six cells; I checked every row's cells, feature splits and variant splits against the table by eye. Table 2 rows are labelled 'Table 2 row k' (k=1..20 from the top) and their Author(year/country) cell is copied into source_reference_in_review; the combined 'Age of onset/gender/Age of diagnosis' cell is split by its header order (not a stacked ' / ' cell). The country in that cell is the publication's (year/country), not stated as the patient's origin, so ethnicity_or_country is 'not reported' for Table 2 rows. Table 2 never prints the gene symbol for its variants, so gene_symbol_as_stated is 'not reported' on those rows (and on the father's and the Eurofever patient's rows, whose sentences name no gene); rows with 'NA' HGVS (rows 1 and 5; NA defined as not reported) get no variant row. '(novel)' after two Table 2 variants was not recorded as a pathogenicity class. The Eurofever registry patient carrying E257G (ref 9) is included as 'ref (9) patient' because the paper gives the variant and ancestry ('all of European descent' for the named group of 16). The mother is included as a tested-negative relative (no variant row). For the father, zygosity, pathogenicity and ACMG were left 'not reported' because the paper states them only for the proband's variant. Patient laboratory values: Hb 116 g/L (ref 118-156) and PLT 560 (ref 167-453) are below/above the printed reference ranges but the paper never calls them anemia or thrombocytosis, so no rows; checklist anemia left 'not reported'. 'Normal blood tests, biochemistry, coagulation' (Jan 2021-Jul 2022) is a whole-investigation normal finding and excludes nothing more specific; only HLA-B27 was recorded. 'No cutaneous lesions (acne or PG)' was used to exclude acne and PG only; hidradenitis/abscess left 'not reported'. Contradictions/inconsistencies in the paper: genetic identification is dated 'At age 7 (2021)' and 'January 2021' in the text but Table 1 places whole-exome sequencing in the Jan 2021 - Jul 2022 row; the definitive diagnosis is dated Apr 2023 in Table 1 but '2022–2026' in the Discussion; the treatment section gives prednisone 0.5 mg/kg/day and methotrexate 15 mg/m²/week after diagnosis while Table 1 says doses unknown; the Discussion says 'normalized CRP/ESR' while Table 1 gives hs-CRP 15 mg/L and ESR 62 mm/h at 5 months; the Dec 2020 knee MRI is 'suggestive of pyogenic arthritis' in the text and 'suggestive of septic arthritis' in Table 1. Abstract calls the Eurofever registry patients 16 'all of European descent'; Discussion says the E257G patient was from an Italian cohort.

span: He underwent three surgical debridements between 2018 and 2021 for suspected septic arthritis; all intraoperative cultures were negative. Multiple courses of antibiotics failed to control his symptoms.
Following diagnosis, treatment with prednisone (0.5 mg/kg/day), methotrexate (15 mg/m²/week), and adalimumab (40 mg every other week) provided only partial and transient improvement.
Weekly oral methotrexate 5 mg + folic acid 10 mg, meloxicam 5.625 mg qd, prednisolone acetate 2.5 mg qd, combined with traditional Chinese medicine

IL-1 inhibitors (anakinra 100 mg/day or canakinumab 2 mg/kg every 4 weeks) were not accessible owing to financial constraints.
